html:
The Visigothic Kingdom was the realm of the Visigoths in southwest Gaul and then in the Iberian Peninsula, from 418 to the early 700s. On the map for 600 and 700 it covers nearly all of Spain and Portugal.

Rome first settled the Visigoths in Aquitaine under King Wallia, with Toulouse as their capital. After Clovis and the Franks beat them at the Battle of Vouillé in 507, they lost almost all of Gaul and moved their centre to Toledo. Kings such as Leovigild brought most of the peninsula under one rule. In 589 King Reccared gave up Arian Christianity for the Catholic faith of his subjects. Bishop Isidore of Seville wrote an encyclopedia that Europe copied for centuries.

The kingdom was torn by fights over the throne. In 711 an army under Tariq ibn Ziyad crossed from Africa, King Roderic was killed, and within a few years the Umayyad conquest was complete. Only in the far north did Christian rule survive, in Asturias.
